citeAs: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao (2025). RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv:2505.12224.
creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Xiamen University, Harbin Institute of Technology Shenzhen)
description: RoboFAC dataset is a large-scale and diverse dataset for question-answering on robot failure videos, comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. It covers six types of robotic failures across three hierarchical levels (task planning, motion planning, and execution control), with eight question types targeting task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction. The dataset includes 14 simulated tasks and 6 real-world tasks, with diverse backgrounds and camera viewpoints.
name: RoboFAC dataset
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All GPT-4o generated annotations were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality. For evaluation, GPT-4 was configured with a temperature of 0.2 and Top-P of 1.0 to ensure fairness and consistency in scoring results.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: GPT-4o (for generating reference answers for failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction questions); manual human review for quality control
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Raw data was annotated to construct video-based QA samples for eight question types. For five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from the textual description associated with the video. For the remaining three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction), both the video and its corresponding textual description were used as inputs to GPT-4o to generate reference answers using a structured prompt. All GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality. Five question templates were provided per question type, and one template was randomly sampled per QA pair.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset introduces variations in backgrounds and camera viewpoints to account for diversity of deployment settings in real-world robotics, aiming to facilitate development of models with better visual generalization capabilities. The training set is drawn exclusively from simulated data (60K QA pairs), while the test set includes both simulated and real-world data, with two real-world tasks (InsertCylinder and PlaceCube) never seen during training, enabling assessment of sim-to-real transfer.
rai:dataCollection: Simulation data was collected for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Expert policies were defined by specifying target end-effector poses for each substage, and failure data was generated by replacing the expert policy with code snippets that produce erroneous trajectories at selected substages. Real-world data was collected for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. Each video was accompanied by a corresponding textual description including the substage where failure occurred, the taxonomy of failure, and a detailed textual explanation of the error.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of robotic failure and success videos from simulation (ManiSkill environment) and real-world (SO-100 robotic arm via teleoperation), along with corresponding textual descriptions. The dataset includes 8,960 failure trajectories and 1,160 successful trajectories from simulation, and 480 failure trajectories and 122 successful trajectories from real-world executions. Each video is paired with a descriptive text noting the substage of failure, failure taxonomy, and detailed error explanation; for pose perturbation failures, the perturbed pose is also recorded.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Experiments, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The current integration of the RoboFAC model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless. The success rate in real-world tasks remains subject to further enhancement, largely due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions. The model is applied exclusively to VLA models in this work, and more targeted correction strategies for hierarchical policies have not yet been explored.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual data cleaning was performed on simulation data: since motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions, thorough manual data cleaning was performed and approximately 75% of the collected data was retained.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables development of robotic systems that can detect, analyze, and recover from failures, improving the robustness and reliability of robotic manipulation in open-world scenarios. This supports safer and more capable deployment of VLA-based robotic systems in real-world environments.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating multimodal large language models for robotic failure analysis and correction; benchmarking models on task understanding, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating, failure explanation, and failure correction (high-level and low-level) in robotic manipulation; integrating as an external critic model in VLA-based robotic control pipelines to provide real-time correction instructions for failure recovery.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o was used to generate reference answers for three question types (failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction) using structured prompts combining video and textual descriptions. GPT-4 was also used as a scoring agent for evaluation, rating model responses on correctness, relevance, and completeness.
